title: xEdge Core Configuration
description: Schema for the core section of xedge.yaml (FR-CM-001). Per-driver schemas are loaded and validated independently by the driver framework (FR-DF-004).

schema_version.description: Config schema version, e.g. '0.1'. Used by the migration tool (NFR-M-003).

data_dir.description: Root directory for all persistent state (system-architecture.md §6.4). Every other persistent path defaults to a subdirectory of this one: store.directory -> <data_dir>/store, config_management.history_directory -> <data_dir>/config-history, plus the Web UI auth/audit state and the fleet device token. Set this one value to relocate all of them; the individual path settings still override it where a deployment needs to split them across volumes.

interval_seconds.description: Must kick at least once per 30s per NFR-R-005; default kicks at 2x that margin.

sntp.description: In-app SNTP client and sync-status reporting (Sprint C3, XEDGE-437; CRD §4.8). Off by default — most deployments already rely on the OS's own NTP client (HLR ASM-001); enable this to have xEdge independently verify and report sync status in the Web UI. Queries time only; does not set the system clock.

servers.description: Tried in order each sync cycle; the first to answer wins. Each entry is `host` (standard port 123) or `host:port`.

sync_interval_seconds.description: How often to re-query. A 10s floor guards against flooding a public NTP pool from a misconfigured value.

timezone.description: IANA timezone name, for displaying local time in the Web UI only — xEdge's own timestamps (FR-DP-001) remain UTC regardless of this setting.

stale_after_seconds.description: How long since the last successful sync before sync-status reporting flags it stale.

system_tags.description: Per-driver-instance synthetic health/statistics tags (status, status_time, tag_count, read rates, ...) published under each instance's `_system/` sub-namespace, alongside its real tags.

drivers.description: Driver instances. Each driver's `config` and `tag_groups` are validated against that driver type's own schema (FR-DF-004) — not enumerated here in Sprint 1.

northbound.description: Northbound MQTT + Sparkplug B connector (FR-NB-001..FR-NB-006). Only a single connector is supported in Sprint 3; FR-NB-005 (>=3 simultaneous connectors) is later-sprint scope.

publish_interval_seconds.description: How often the dispatcher drains the ring buffer and publishes an NDATA batch.

publisher_type.description: Sprint C5, XEDGE-451 (CRD §4.10 'own payload structure'). 'sparkplug_b' (default, unchanged): MqttSparkplugConnector, birth/death/sequence-numbered protobuf. 'generic_json': GenericMqttPublisher, configurable plain-JSON topic/payload -- see the generic_json_* fields below, which that mode alone consumes.

tls_enabled.description: Sprint C4, XEDGE-441 (CRD §4.10; closes finding F-10 and SR 3.1 of the SL-1 gap analysis): connect to the broker over TLS instead of plaintext. Independent of the fleet agent's own certificate (XEDGE-442) -- a customer's MQTT broker is typically a separate trust domain from xEdge's fleet PKI.

tls_ca_certs_path.description: CA bundle verifying the broker's certificate. Omit to use the system trust store (a publicly-trusted broker certificate).

tls_certfile_path.description: Client certificate for mTLS to the broker, if it requires one. Requires tls_keyfile_path unless this file contains both the certificate and key.

tls_insecure.description: Disables broker *hostname* verification only (not certificate validity) -- for a broker reachable only by an IP its certificate can't reasonably enumerate in advance.

generic_json_topic_template.description: publisher_type: generic_json only. {tag_id} is substituted per message in 'per_tag' mode; must not appear in 'batch' mode, where every batch publishes to this one fixed topic.

generic_json_payload_mode.description: publisher_type: generic_json only. 'per_tag': one MQTT message per tag. 'batch': one message containing a JSON array of every tag in the batch.

generic_json_field_names.description: publisher_type: generic_json only. Renames output JSON keys, e.g. {"tag_id": "name", "value": "val"}. Keys not overridden here keep their default name (tag_id, value, timestamp, quality).

opcua_server.description: OPC UA server exposing active tags (FR-UA-001..FR-UA-007). MVP: no security policy beyond None, no user auth — see xedge.northbound.opcua_server module docstring.

store.description: Store-and-forward: RAM ring buffer (hot tier) spilling to SQLite WAL (cold tier) on overflow (FR-SF-001..FR-SF-003, ADR-003).

ram_max_depth.description: FR-SF-001: samples held per stream before spilling to the cold tier.

purge_interval_seconds.description: How often the retention purge sweep runs.

config_management.description: Config hot-reload and version history (FR-CM-002, FR-CM-005, FR-CM-006).

poll_interval_seconds.description: How often xedge.yaml's mtime is checked for changes.

max_versions.description: FR-CM-006: last 10 versions retained by default.

api.description: Read-only REST API v1 (FR-CM-003): status, driver list, running config. No auth in the MVP, so it defaults to loopback-only — see xedge.api.server module docstring before setting `host` to anything broader.

host.description: Loopback-only by default since there's no auth yet. Set to a specific interface address (not 0.0.0.0) if the API needs to be reachable from elsewhere on the OT network.

tls.description: Server-side TLS for the Web UI/REST API (Sprint 13, XEDGE-107/280 — partial scope: HTTPS only, not client-certificate/mutual-TLS enforcement). A self-signed certificate is auto-generated on first boot if `cert_path`/`key_path` don't already hold one.

cert_path.description: Defaults to a file alongside the Web UI's users.json/session_key if not set.

key_path.description: Defaults to a file alongside the Web UI's users.json/session_key if not set.

tracing.description: OpenTelemetry distributed tracing (Sprint 16, XEDGE-126/127). Defaults off — a TracerProvider with nowhere to send spans is pure overhead, and the dev collector stack (Grafana/Tempo/Loki) is out of scope for this pass. When enabled with no otlp_endpoint set, spans print to the console instead of going nowhere.

otlp_endpoint.description: e.g. http://localhost:4318/v1/traces (OTLP/HTTP). If unset while enabled, spans export to the console instead.

device_id.description: Optional resource attribute identifying this device in traces/metrics.

dashboard_url.description: Optional Grafana/collector dashboard URL — shown as a Web UI footer link if set (XEDGE-283); hidden entirely otherwise.

metrics.description: Prometheus metrics exposition on GET /metrics (Sprint 16, XEDGE-128/130). Defaults on — the endpoint is cheap to serve and needs no external collector to be useful.

rate_limit.description: Per-client-IP request rate limiting (Sprint 18, XEDGE-144/285 — IEC 62443 SR 7.1). Covers the REST API and every Web UI route identically. Defaults on.

alarms.description: Alarm engine v2 (Sprint 31, XEDGE-224/225/228): threshold (high/high_high/low/low_low) and rate-of-change alarm detection, evaluated in the pipeline after scaling. A tag with a rule is 'alarm-tier' (backpressure instead of eviction, independently retained) regardless of whether it is currently alarming — see xedge.core.alarms module docstring. Defaults off.

retention_duration_seconds.description: XEDGE-225/228: alarm-tier retention, independent of (and normally longer than) store.retention_duration_seconds. Default 30 days.

assets.description: Asset Management (Sprint C6, XEDGE-460; ADR-010): a metadata and grouping layer over the existing driver-first model -- an asset's parameters *reference* existing tags (instance_id/tag_id, via parameters[].tag_ref); they never define new ones. Referential integrity (every tag_ref must resolve to a real driver/tag) is checked beyond what this schema alone expresses, on every config apply -- see xedge.core.assets.validate_asset_references. Defaults to an empty list; a deployment with no assets behaves exactly as it did before this section existed.

enabled.description: Presentational only (ADR-010 §4): suppresses this asset from asset-scoped views/reports. Does NOT stop the backing driver instances, which may also back parameters on other assets -- stopping data collection remains a driver-level operation (POST /api/v1/drivers/{id}/disable).

gateway_id.description: Optional, soft reference to a Fleet Manager device id (ADR-010 §4) -- never validated locally against the fleet registry, which is a separate system this device may have no connection to at all (fleet.enabled: false is fully supported).

tag_ref.description: instance_id/tag_id of an existing tag under drivers[] -- a reference, never a new tag definition. Checked for referential integrity on every config apply.

store.description: ADR-010 §3: false suppresses this tag from cold-store spill (RAM-tier/live visibility is unaffected). If the same tag_ref is also referenced elsewhere (this or another asset) with store: true, that wins.

smtp.description: SMTP client (Sprint C6, XEDGE-466; CRD §4.7/FR-SC-002): email notifications on alarm transitions, plus periodic summary reports. Wired directly to the Alarm Engine v2 (Sprint 31) rather than behind a generic notification-channel interface -- SMTP is the only channel this delivery's CRD calls for. Defaults off.

tls_mode.description: "starttls" upgrades a plaintext connection (the common port-587 case); "smtps" is TLS from the first byte (port 465) -- two different protocols on the wire, not one feature with an on/off switch.

tls_ca_certs_path.description: CA bundle verifying the server's certificate, for starttls and smtps alike. Omit to use the system trust store (a publicly-trusted mail relay); set for a self-signed or private-CA internal relay.

alarm_notifications.description: One email per alarm raise or clear (an ACTIVE -> ACTIVE_ACKED ack alone sends nothing -- the recipient already knows). A shelved alarm (xedge.core.alarms.AlarmEngine.shelve) never notifies either, for as long as it's shelved.

scheduled_reports.description: Each entry gets its own independent task/schedule -- one report firing on its interval never blocks or waits on another. A report's alarm summary is a live snapshot of currently-active alarms at send time, not a historical digest of everything that transitioned since the last report.

include_asset_ids.description: Resolves to every one of that asset's parameters' tag_ref at send time -- not a snapshot taken when the report was configured, so it stays current as an asset's parameters change.

fleet.description: Fleet agent (Sprint 29, XEDGE-210/213; reworked Sprint C4, XEDGE-442, ADR-013 §3): periodic heartbeat to a separate Fleet Manager service, and pull-based config push (this device applies a pending config through the existing hot-reload file-write path, then reports the result on the next heartbeat). Defaults off. Enrollment (one-time, over manager_url) exchanges a single-use join token and a locally-generated CSR for a CA-signed device certificate; heartbeat/config-pull (over device_manager_url) then authenticate with that certificate plus a device token, both persisted locally alongside the never-transmitted private key.

manager_url.description: Base URL of the Fleet Manager's enrollment/admin port, e.g. https://fleet-manager.local:8090. Used once, for /enroll.

device_manager_url.description: Base URL of the Fleet Manager's mTLS device port, e.g. https://fleet-manager.local:8091. Used for every heartbeat after enrollment; required when fleet.enabled is true.

device_id.description: Stable identity this device enrolls under; required when fleet.enabled is true.

join_token.description: Single-use, time-limited token an operator provisioned for this specific device_id (Fleet Manager admin API: POST /api/v1/fleet/join-tokens). Consumed by /enroll; the manager then issues a device certificate and device token, persisted locally alongside the device's own private key.

heartbeat_interval_seconds.description: XEDGE-210: how often the agent reports identity/health and polls for a pending config push.

verify_tls.description: Governs only the one-time enrollment call to manager_url, before this device has any knowledge of the fleet CA. Set false to accept a self-signed/unverified Fleet Manager certificate at that step (matches xedge-cli's --insecure posture for local/dev deployments). The device_manager_url connection is always verified against the fleet CA certificate enrollment returned, regardless of this setting.

cert_rotation_threshold_days.description: ADR-013 §3/XEDGE-443: the agent re-keys once its certificate has fewer than this many days left before expiry, checked once per heartbeat. Default gives a 90-day-validity certificate (the Fleet Manager's own --cert-validity-days default) 60 days of retry margin -- well clear of the Web UI's 14-day 'expires soon' warning, which should not normally fire at all.

mqtt_broker.description: Embedded MQTT broker (Sprint C5, XEDGE-453/454; ADR-012 §3): a listening service other MQTT clients (SCADA, cloud integrations) connect to -- the reverse of northbound.mqtt above, which is an outbound client connecting to an *external* broker. Defaults off. See xedge.northbound.mqtt_broker module docstring for why mTLS is not offered as an access-control option here (amqtt's cafile always sets CERT_OPTIONAL, never CERT_REQUIRED) -- username/password plus topic ACLs is the supported model instead.

host.description: A broker must accept connections from other devices/clients on the network, unlike the loopback-only REST API default.

allow_anonymous.description: XEDGE-454: off by default. When false, every connecting client must authenticate as one of `users` below.

users.description: Consulted only when allow_anonymous is false. Hashed (sha512_crypt via passlib) into a generated password file on startup, never persisted in plaintext by xEdge itself -- but this config value is, same as fleet.join_token above.

publish_acl.description: username -> allowed publish topic patterns (ordinary MQTT +/# wildcards), e.g. {"sensor01": ["telemetry/sensor01/#"]}. Left empty (default) while subscribe_acl is also empty, no ACL plugin loads at all and any authenticated user may publish anywhere. IMPORTANT (verified against amqtt's own topic_checking plugin source, not documented by amqtt itself): the moment EITHER this or subscribe_acl is non-empty, the ACL plugin loads for both directions -- and unlike publish, subscribe has no 'empty means unrestricted' carve-out. Setting only publish_acl denies every subscribe from every user. If you only want to restrict publishing, list every legitimate subscriber in subscribe_acl too (a ["#"] entry grants that user unrestricted subscribe access).

subscribe_acl.description: username -> allowed subscribe topic patterns, same wildcard syntax as publish_acl. Left empty while publish_acl is also empty, unrestricted (see publish_acl's description above for the asymmetry once either dict is non-empty: an empty subscribe_acl at that point means zero subscribe access for everyone, not unrestricted).

snmp_agent.description: SNMP agent (Sprint C8, XEDGE-482; ADR-012 §2): xEdge itself pollable by the customer's NMS -- the reverse of a snmp_client driver instance, which polls an external device. Defaults off. Exposes standard MIB-II plus a live driver-status table and alarm-state counts under a placeholder OID subtree -- see xedge.northbound.snmp_agent's module docstring for why (no IANA-registered Private Enterprise Number exists for xEdge yet; XEDGE-DR-001 Q-8).

host.description: An agent must accept polls from the customer's NMS on the network, unlike the loopback-only REST API default.

community.description: SNMPv1/v2c community string this agent accepts. Read-only: this agent never accepts SNMP SET from the network (XEDGE-DR-001 Q-9) -- the community only gates GET/GETNEXT/GETBULK.

snmp_notify.description: SNMP TRAP/INFORM originator (Sprint C8, XEDGE-483), wired to the Alarm Engine: one notification per alarm raise or clear, same ack/shelve suppression rules as smtp.alarm_notifications (an ACTIVE -> ACTIVE_ACKED ack alone sends nothing; a shelved alarm never notifies while shelved). See xedge.core.snmp_notify's module docstring for the placeholder-PEN OIDs this sends under, and for why notify_type: trap can only ever report 'sent', never 'delivered' (RFC 1905 fire-and-forget UDP, no acknowledgement) -- use notify_type: inform wherever delivery confirmation actually matters.

v3_priv_protocol.description: Requires v3_auth_protocol != 'none', same RFC 3414 rule as the snmp_client driver's identical field.

notify_type.description: trap: fire-and-forget, no delivery confirmation possible even in principle. inform: the sender waits for a real acknowledgement, so a send failure here means an unreachable/non-responding destination, not just 'we transmitted a packet'.
